text:
harper: FYI hitting a weird class of failure in prod — when the auth token refresh happens mid-stream, the edge proxy sometimes closes the connection instead of letting the backend finish and returning the partial stream. Seen it twice across two clusters. Anyone familiar with the interaction between token refresh, rate limiter, and graceful drain?
ingrid: hmm interesting. do you have logs or an example request id?
harper: request id: rq_0a9c3f, snippet below. looks like: auth refresh at t+2s, client still reading, then rate-limiter hits an active-conn quota and we close.
```
[edge] 2026-11-03T12:01:02Z rq_0a9c3f INFO: incoming stream -> routed to runtime-a
[edge] 2026-11-03T12:01:04Z rq_0a9c3f INFO: refresh token handshake started (user=svc-analytics)
[edge] 2026-11-03T12:01:04Z rq_0a9c3f WARN: token refresh required midstream
[edge] 2026-11-03T12:01:05Z rq_0a9c3f ERROR: rate-limiter active_conn_quota_exceeded (limit=150)
[edge] 2026-11-03T12:01:05Z rq_0a9c3f INFO: closing connection: active_conn_quota_exceeded
```
ben-r: that error sequence suggests the rate-limiter counts the connection while it's in token refresh state and treats the refresh handshake as a blocking window. we should probably special-case token refresh to be non-counted or to use a separate soft quota.
santi: Agree with ben. Two tradeoffs: 1) exempting auth refresh reduces protection against fanout storms where refresh loops cause many held connections; 2) making it a soft quota with short backoff increases complexity but preserves user-facing streams.
harper: For context, these are long-polling streaming completions (not tiny requests). Clients keep the connection open; refresh is infrequent but tends to coincide with bursty deploys. We can't drop them mid-stream—clients expect deterministic partial responses.
ingrid: Could we instead change the lifecycle so that token refresh is performed out-of-band: i.e., edge keeps the connection sticky and opens a transient control channel to auth to refresh credentials without mutating the primary stream's resource accounting?
santi: That's basically decoupling the auth refresh from the connection lease. Implementation sketch: signal refresh via control channel; only if auth fails completely do we tear down. Meanwhile, the rate-limiter should decrement active_conn during short blocking ops (<250ms) if flagged as refresh.
harper: Implementation sketch looks good. We also need to consider retries: if a refresh fails and we retry auth, we shouldn't increase hedging or hedges shouldn't count additional connections against tenant quota.
ben-r: Right — hedging on auth should be detached from tenant active_conn accounting. Otherwise you can accidentally trigger tenant throttles by the platform's own retries.
infra-bot: deploy queued: edge-proxy v3.12.1 -> canary started in us-west-2 at 2026-11-03T12:10:00Z
ingrid: Concrete proposal: 3 changes (short + backward compatible):
- Mark token refresh window with a RefreshLease flag. Rate-limiter uses separate small buffer (soft_refresh_buffer = 50) before cutting.
- Treat refresh retries as internal calls: they get a transient internal tag that exempts them from tenant quota accounting; still counted against global system safety budget.
- Add a graceful-close policy: if a refresh occurs midstream, prefer to continue streaming to client for up to 500ms while auth resolves; only escalate to a 401/close if auth conclusively fails.
harper: I like that. Any obvious backwards-compat pitfalls?
santi: A few: cache poisoning risk if refresh path is privileged; instrumentation must clearly separate internal vs tenant metrics. Also, soft_refresh_buffer must be tuned per-cluster — 50 might be too big for small tenants.
ben-r: Also watch out for tracing: we need to surface the refresh lifecycle in traces so SRE can correlate drops to refresh windows. Add a span on the main trace with tag refresh=true.
ingrid: I'll draft an RFC PR with small state-machine changes to IngressConn: states = {Active, RefreshPending, Draining, Closed}. RefreshPending is offloaded to control channel.
harper: Thanks — please add a unit test for race where refresh triggers and rate-limiter concurrently decides to drop. We saw a reproducible in the chaos-run: reproduce steps attached in the RFC.
santi: One more thought: for dedicated customers with strict quotas we might expose a config flag: refresh_policy = {strict, soft, off} so enterprise can choose. Default to soft.
harper: OK let's proceed. Ingrid, can you create the RFC and tag eng-runtime + eng-sre + security for review? I'll queue a canary after the RFC lands. :thumbsup:
ingrid: on it, I'll make the PR in ~1h and include logs + test harness.
ben-r: ping me for review, I can help with rate-limiter adjustments.
infra-bot: canary rollout event: edge-proxy v3.12.1 10% us-west-2 started 2026-11-03T12:13:00Z
